claims.statement: RFC 3986 §3.2 defines the URI authority component as [userinfo@]host[:port], meaning that in 'user@host', 'host' is the string following the '@' delimiter, not preceding it.
Resolving DNS during validation and resolving DNS again during HTTP socket connection creates a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerability exploitable via DNS rebinding (TTL: 0s).
claims.scope: Applications that validate hostnames via DNS resolution but pass the original hostname string to the HTTP client sink

claims.statement: Network-segmented internal microservices and cloud metadata endpoints grant ambient authorization based on source IP address rather than requiring per-request cryptographic authentication.
claims.scope: Cloud instances and private VPC networks relying solely on perimeter network controls

claims.statement: AWS IMDSv2 requires a PUT request with a custom header to acquire a session token, thereby neutralizing simple GET-only SSRF primitives. Additionally, the default hop limit (TTL=1) on the token request prevents it from crossing a network boundary — so SSRF from inside a container cannot reach the metadata endpoint even if the primitive supports PUT with custom headers.
claims.scope: AWS EC2 instances with IMDSv2 enabled. The hop limit defense specifically applies when the SSRF originates from a container or crosses a network boundary.

claims.statement: Server-side HTTP client libraries that follow HTTP 3xx redirects automatically will connect to the target specified in the Location header without re-applying application-layer input allowlists.
claims.scope: Default configurations of standard HTTP client libraries (e.g. requests, curl, urllib)

claims.statement: Some socket libraries resolve alternative IP integer representations (such as dword/decimal 2130706433 or octal 017700000001) to 127.0.0.1, bypassing naive regex-based IP blocklists. However, support varies: glibc accepts octal/hex/decimal, but musl libc (Alpine Linux/Docker), Go's net.ParseIP(), and Python's ipaddress module do not.
claims.scope: glibc-based resolvers (Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL). Does NOT reliably apply to musl-based systems (Alpine Linux), Go standard library, or Python ipaddress module.
